summary: Today’s pulse tracks US midterm elections 2026 live: Americans go to the polls to decide control of Congress, Latest Sarah J Maas book becomes UK’s fastest-selling adult fantasy novel, and NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms. Across Guardian and Ars Technica, the strongest repeated signals are trump, novel, and against. In the background, Seven reported bomb threats against European flights confirmed as false alarms – as it happened and Buttons are back and storage is king when it comes to car interiors keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: US midterm elections 2026 live: Americans go to the polls to decide control of Congress
headlines.description: Voters are casting their ballots across the US in a referendum on Donald Trump’s agenda Here are some of the key voter issues shaping the US midterm elections: The economy : Despite Trump’s 2024 campaign pledge to tackle affordability issues, the economy consistently ranks as voters’ top concern. Iran : Trump’s decision to go to war with the Tehran regime has exacerbated economic worries. Iran’s retaliatory decision to close the strait of Hormuz has driven up gasoline prices for US motorists. It also represents a breach of his pledge to end the US’s supposed addiction to “forever wars”. Immigration : Enforcement and closing the border remains a signature issue for Trump. He repeatedly boasts of the impact of his closure of the southern border as one of his biggest achievements, making comparisons with the performance of Joe Biden. AI and datacenters: AI has emerged as a key campaign issue, with surveys showing a majority of voters holding negative views on it, even as Trump champions its development and attempts to rename it “super intelligence”.

headlines.title: Latest Sarah J Maas book becomes UK’s fastest-selling adult fantasy novel
headlines.description: A Court of Splintered Harmony also records biggest single week of sales since Harper Lee’s Go Set a Watchman in 2015 Sarah J Maas’s long-awaited return to her bestselling romantasy series has smashed UK sales records, with A Court of Splintered Harmony becoming the fastest-selling adult fantasy novel since accurate records began in 1998. The novel, the sixth in Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses (Acotar) series and her first return to it in more than five years, sold 188,914 copies in the UK between publication day on 27 October and 31 October, according to NielsenIQ BookData. That also makes it the fastest-selling hardback novel since Dan Brown’s Inferno, which sold 229,000 copies in its first week in 2013.

headlines.title: Panel rules out further inquiry into sexual harassment claims against Lib Dem peer Chris Rennard
headlines.description: Party leader Ed Davey ‘disappointed and upset’ at decision by independent panel after claims original investigation was flawed The Liberal Democrat peer Chris Rennard has been told there will be no further investigation into sexual harassment allegations made against him, after an independent panel concluded it could not reopen the claim. The party leader, Ed Davey, said he was “disappointed and upset” by the conclusion, having suspended Rennard from the party after an investigation was reopened earlier this year amid claims a previous inquiry was flawed.

headlinePool.title: ‘Well-known individual’ fails in bid for injunction against Guardian and ITN
headlinePool.description: Person’s anonymity remains in place subject to any appeal against high court decision A “well-known individual” has failed in his attempt to stop two media organisations from publishing allegations of inappropriate sexual activities towards young women, the high court has ruled. The legal team for the anonymous individual, known in court only as PPT, had claimed he was “highly likely” to attempt suicide if the Guardian and ITN published the allegations, which he denies.

headlinePool.title: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
headlinePool.description: Planes in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy have been checked for explosives following separate threats.

headlinePool.title: Google will let schools skip AI tools, but they have to give up search, too
headlinePool.description: Google will offer schools AI tools that purportedly don't give away the answers.

headlinePool.title: US man charged with mailing hundreds of letters containing powder to officials before midterms
headlinePool.description: Oklahoma man accused of sending letters with white nonhazardous powder before 2024 and 2026 elections Federal authorities have charged an Oklahoma man with sending hundreds of letters containing nonhazardous white powder to public officials before the 2024 and 2026 elections. The powders turned out to be yeast or flour, though not all letters had been fully tested, the FBI said in a court filing made public on Tuesday.

headlinePool.title: UK makes huge aid cuts to Commonwealth nations despite warm words at Chogm summit
headlinePool.description: Nations in the group fare worse than others, with funding for nature projects especially hard hit even as climate crisis intensifies global need The UK government has slashed overseas aid to Commonwealth countries, the Guardian can reveal, in contrast to the warm words for the group from King Charles and the prime minister, Andy Burnham , this week. Amid sharp cuts in the UK’s aid budget overall, the Commonwealth has fared poorly, an analysis of the most recent and projected aid figures, seen by the Guardian, has shown.

headlinePool.title: Man who drugged and raped wife found many men ‘whose fantasy is an unconscious woman’, court told
headlinePool.description: Nine men stand trial in Manchester accused of participating in abuse at couple’s home in Stockport, or encouraging it online The Stockport man who drugged, raped and sexually assaulted his wife personally found a large number of the “many, many men whose fantasy is an unconscious and unresponsive woman”, a court has heard. Nine men are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street crown court, accused of either participating in the abuse, which took place at the couple’s home, or encouraging it online.

headlinePool.title: Pardoned January 6 participant charged over alleged threats to kill federal judges
headlinePool.description: Cleveland Meredith arrested after allegedly posting a call to execute all judges involved in 2021 US Capitol attack trials A man pardoned by Donald Trump for participating in January 6 attack on the US Capitol and threatening to kill the then house speaker, Nancy Pelosi , is facing new charges for threatening to kill federal judges that presided over his and other cases arising from the violent anti-government clash. Cleveland Meredith, from North Carolina , was arrested on Monday over a Facebook post in April that allegedly read: “ALL J6 Federal JUDGES will be EXECUTED!”

headlinePool.title: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats
headlinePool.description: Unclear if series of incidents affecting two UK departures and a number of Ryanair services among others are connected Europe live – latest updates At least seven planes around Europe were searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats to passenger flights on Tuesday. Two UK departures and a number of Ryanair flights were threatened in what the UK government called “malicious hoaxes”, after all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.

headlinePool.title: Food suppliers in UK hit by cyber-attacks after freezers targeted in Europe
headlinePool.description: Cybersecurity experts say national impact ‘minimal’ but incidents may represent the ‘foothills’ of a wider threat Food suppliers in the UK have been hit by cyber-attacks after hackers raised the temperatures of supermarket freezers across Europe. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NSCS) said it was working with the affected companies but the national impact was minimal.
